performance.round1_hypothesis: GPU fill rate / post-processing — REFUTED on the owner's M1 (fx=off gave only some improvement)
performance.round2: shipped a subtractive diagnostic harness instead of a second guess: src/diag/diagnostics.ts + DiagOverlay.tsx; flags ?diag=1 ?bench=1 ?dpr=N ?field=off ?core=off ?feed=off ?anim=off, all OFF by default
performance.cpu_gpu_method: wrap renderer.render() and time it against the frame interval; renderMs approx frameMs = CPU-bound, renderMs << frameMs = limited elsewhere; EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 used when the driver exposes it
ruled_out: per-lead React components (leads are one THREE.Points draw call)
draw-call count (29-45 per frame at every book size)
Three.js object-update cost (render() CPU is 0.3-0.5ms in EVERY configuration)
performance.round3: bench median was the vsync interval quantised (58.8fps/17.0ms in all 9 configs, incl. field=off); added distribution p95/p99/max, >20/33/50/100ms buckets, longtask, Event Timing input latency, per-path spans, and scripted pointer + drag sweeps
performance.measured_js_at_4892: revisionWalk 1.7-2.1ms x ~9/s; Points.raycast 0.094ms scanning all 4892 (confirmed O(n), 596824 points / 122 calls); settled frame loop 0.063ms; ingest 0.055ms incl subscribers; TOTAL ~2.7% of one core
ruled_out_round3: the full-book revision walk (real waste, wrong magnitude)
performance.round4: production build measures HEALTHY on the owner's M1 (drag sweep 901 frames, p99 23ms, max 28ms, ZERO frames >33ms, zero long tasks) while the owner still reports grade D — read as the harness measuring the wrong thing, not as the app being fine
performance.dev_vs_prod_measured: app spans identical (revisionWalk 1.79 vs 1.84ms); dev carries ~1.9x the main-thread long-task load (188-196 vs 100-106 tasks) and loads 4.3x slower; the dev penalty lands in React render work that NO instrumented span covers
instrument_defects_known: installLongTaskObserver reports count=0 when observe() throws — Safari has PerformanceObserver but not the longtask entry type, so every '0 long tasks' reading is a FALSE NEGATIVE on Safari
the jank report header does not record build mode (dev vs production), so two pasted reports are indistinguishable without manual labelling
performance.round5: owner is on SAFARI; dev == production subjectively, retiring the build-mode hypothesis. Enumerated the full graphics/compositor stack and found FOUR backdrop-filter:blur() elements layered directly over the live WebGL canvas (.command-row and .command-out at 14px, .uv-clusters and .uv-skills at 6px)
performance.round6: backdrop-filter CONFIRMED as a real but PARTIAL contributor (owner A/B: noticeable improvement, significant lag remains). Safari ~= Chrome subjectively on careful re-comparison, retiring the WebKit-specific hypothesis. Chrome measured numerically worse while feeling the same, and ALL spans scaled together (~3x), so revisionWalk is explicitly not concluded to be the cause. Shipped ?matrix=1: ten cases, one axis each, identical 8s scripted drag, plus per-frame bad-frame correlation (GPU fence vs spans vs long tasks) to classify GPU-bound vs main-thread stalls
round6_harness_bugs_caught: correlation records stored ms=0 because frame duration was computed after `last` was reassigned — every bad-frame bucket was silently empty while the distribution table looked correct. Fixed and re-validated.
?dpr=1 was unverifiable locally (machine is already DPR 1); checked at simulated Retina, drawing buffer 1600x552 -> 800x276 as intended
performance.superseded_hypothesis: CSS backdrop-filter compositing over the WebGL canvas — work that happens AFTER requestAnimationFrame returns and is invisible to every instrument here. First hypothesis consistent with ALL evidence: JS cheap, frame intervals perfect, fx=off partial, field=off/core=off making no difference (a backdrop blur costs the same regardless of what is behind it), dev==prod, Safari-specific severity. UNTESTED — ?backdrop=off decides it in ~1 minute
performance.not_observable_from_js: true presentation time (pixels on glass) in Safari: no frame-timing API, no long-animation-frame, no EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2. GL execution, WebKit compositing, backdrop-filter evaluation and the vsync handoff are all invisible. Best proxies added: polled WebGL2 fenceSync, rAF lateness, input->handler latency
diagnostic_fixes_round5: longtask false negative FIXED — Safari now prints 'LONGTASK OBSERVER UNSUPPORTED', never 'count=0'
BUILD MODE (development/production) now printed in every report via import.meta.env.DEV
capability line: longtask, eventTiming, gpuTimerQuery, fenceSync, GL version, renderer string

?backdrop=off and ?overlay=off toggles, injected as a runtime <style> because the CSS minifier rewrote an authored backdrop-filter override to -webkit- only (would have silently disabled the test in Chrome); shipping stylesheets byte-identical
performance.primary_bottleneck: RESOLVED — CSS backdrop-filter compositing over the live WebGL canvas (primary) plus full-resolution bloom (secondary). Confirmed by the owner's A/B on real hardware, not by this machine's numbers
performance.resolution: round 7 accepted as shipping baseline. Owner verdict on 2020 M1 MacBook Air / Safari: performance DRAMATICALLY SMOOTHER, visual difference TINY and still looks just as good, original lag problem BASICALLY SOLVED
shipping_changes: all four backdrop-filter:blur() layers removed from shipping CSS — zero live backdrop sampling in the built bundle; glass rebuilt from gradient + inset rim + drop shadow at an alpha matched to the blurred original's perceived density
Bloom resolutionScale=0.5 — quarter the fragments, upsampled through the existing mip chain; scene still renders at full DPR 2
performance.do_not_regress: never reintroduce backdrop-filter over the WebGL canvas; do not lower DPR, reduce the 4,892-lead book, simplify or remove the Intelligence Core, or change OrbitControls damping
performance.reference_control: ?legacyfx=1 restores the previous pipeline pixel-for-pixel (mean diff 0, max 0) — preserved
performance.lesson: the bottleneck sat in the compositing stage, which no JavaScript instrument can observe. Frame intervals looked healthy in every round; every subtractive scene toggle returned unchanged because a backdrop blur costs the same regardless of what is behind it; the round-6 matrix on real hardware showed no configuration in distress. What located it was reading the CSS and the owner's subjective A/B
